To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. The temperature of the system is a measure of the average time it takes to process a part through the system.

the throughput time (or the throughput time distribution) of a part in a reentrant supply chain is not a function of the work in progress, but of the phase velocity of the part, which is a function of the phase velocity and the work in progress.

the TPT of reentrant supply chains can be predicted by the following equation: TPT = TPT0 + TPT1 * (1 - exp(-TPT0/TPT1)) where TPT0 is the TPT in the steady state and TPT1 is the temperature of the supply chain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the derivation of kinetic and fluid models of reentrant supply chains and with the analysis of the corresponding macroscopic and microscopic behavior.
the development of new models and methods for the analysis of reentrant supply chains.
the development of a kinetic model for a supply chain which is based on the concept of phase velocities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the kinetic and fluid models presented here provide a better description of the behavior of reentrant supply chains, especially for small systems.
the standard stochastic models are not applicable to reentrant systems.
the temperature and the diffusion coefficient are two independent measures of the system state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stochastic models for supply chain dynamics are based on the concept of a phase velocity, and the kinetic and fluid models are based on the concepts of temperature, and diffusion.
the stochastic phase velocity is the key to understanding supply chains.
the stochastic phase velocity is a measure for the rate at which a system is able to change its state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the temperature is an important parameter for supply chains.
a stochastic phase velocity is a natural extension of standard stochastic models for supply chain analysis.
the temperature is a good measure of how well the system is performing and that diffusion is a good measure for its stability.
